steps.text:
Here's the plan before I build anything:

1. Confirm the sizes on the dimension sheet (cube edge, hinge pin, clearance).
2. Design the 8-cube chain with print-in-place hinges.
3. Check the design against its sizes.
4. Set the P1S, PLA and 0.4 mm nozzle as the target (run.target).
5. Slice the plate. Queuing and starting the print need your OK.

The cube edge is yours. The hinge values are my guesses, so please check them.

dims.label: Hinge clearance gap
dims.note: Guess; gap between moving parts so they do not fuse on the P1S

dims.label: Hinge knuckle length
dims.note: Guess; length of each hinge barrel along the edge

args.part: Infinity cube (8 cubes, print in place)
assumptions: Eight 20 mm cubes in one chain, each joined to the next by a hinge along a shared edge, so the chain folds into the infinity cube.
Hinge pin 4 mm, knuckle 6 mm and clearance 0.3 mm are guesses confirmed on the sheet.
Print in place: each hinge leaves a 0.3 mm gap so the parts move free after printing.
Printed flat as one piece on the P1S, PLA, 0.4 mm nozzle.
questions: A true infinity cube folds in three directions; this plan folds the chain in one plane. Is one-plane folding acceptable for the first version?

steps.text:
I've started the design but stopped partway, so nothing is sliced or queued yet. Only the first 20 mm cube exists in the design. The hinge sizes on the sheet are confirmed, but the hinge joints themselves are not built yet.

A true infinity cube folds in three directions and needs a joint on every shared edge. Building that means many cut and join steps, and I haven't finished them. The closest version I can build with these tools is a one-plane chain: eight 20 mm cubes in a row, each pair joined by a 4 mm hinge pin in a 0.3 mm clearance bore, printed flat in place on the P1S with PLA. It folds like a paper chain, not into a full cube.

Should I continue with the one-plane chain, or do you want to wait while I work out the three-direction joints?
